answer: One concrete defense is hardware-anchored identity attestation: before joining, an agent's secure enclave must return a remote-attested quote that binds its identity to a single physical chip, and the economy admits only one active identity per attested device. Minting a thousand sybils then demands a thousand real pieces of silicon, not a free software fork. There is no velvet shortcut: every fake must fund its own hardware, so a sybil swarm's voyage stalls at the cost of machines it can never clone, an anchor no copy can lift.
